items.title: NASA X-59 Explainer: Science of Sonic Booms
items.content_text: The most common misconception about sonic booms is that they’re just the sound created at the moment when an aircraft “breaks the sound barrier.” In reality, a sonic boom is continuous, the audible evidence of invisible pressure waves forming as an aircraft travels faster than sound. As these waves travel toward the ground, they can merge, creating an explosive bang heard by everyone the aircraft passes over.  Sonic booms have been a problem since aircraft first began exceeding the speed of soun

items.content_text: Gaia23braL b is a gas giant exoplanet that orbits a K-type star. Its mass is 1.63 Jupiters, it takes 12.1 years to complete one orbit of its star, and is 4.847 AU from its star. Its discovery was announced in 2026. The post Gaia23braL b appeared first on NASA Science .

items.title: TOI-4427 b
